Subject: StrataGrid site questionnaire and initial constraints

Hi Rishi and team,

Thanks again for taking this on. Attached is our completed site compatibility spreadsheet (site_compat_matrix.xlsx). High-level constraints to note before we sync:

- Air-gapped operations in Production (no direct internet egress from prod racks).
- Egress out allowed through a single vetted proxy pair in our DMZ (TLS inspection).
- On-prem HSM present for key storage (Thales payshield equivalent) available on management VLAN.
- Two colo rooms (A / B) separated by different UPS/PDUs; we can allocate up to 3 server racks (10U each reserved for this project).
- Local NVMe available per node;_central SAN is iSCSI-backed with replication across rooms but has ~8ms write latency in worst case.
- K8s baseline v1.28 required for our other infra.

Open questions for your preflight: any mandatory public endpoints? recommended nodepool breakdown given GPU density? suggestions for KV cache sizing vs model weight storage?

Also looping ops-manager@stratagrid.com for datacenter scheduling.

Thanks,
Emily Park
Platform Ops Lead
StrataGrid

Emily — thanks for the spreadsheet and the clear constraints. We can work within an air-gapped production, but a few clarifying items will help us size the cluster and storage correctly before the architecture review: 

1) Egress proxy: is mutual TLS to the proxy supported from a host agent? will the proxy allow long-lived outbound connections for our control-plane tunnel (typically a TLS reverse-tunnel)?
2) HSM integration: can your ops team provision a KMS endpoint reachable from the management VLAN only, or do we need an HSM appliance directly on the control-plane hosts?
3) Rack power/thermal: GPUs planned per rack? you mentioned 4x GPUs per 10U earlier in the doc — can you confirm GPU model families?
4) Backup window: how often are cross-room SAN snapshots permitted (hourly/daily)?

Preliminary nodepool thought (subject to confirmation):
- control-plane (3 x m6-standard-equivalent, non-GPU) — control plane and etcd, pinned to management VLAN, low-latency LAN access to HSM/KMS.
- inference-gpu (6–9 x rtx-class nodes initially) — local NVMe for KV cache (fast ephemeral), larger blockstore for model weights (CSI to iSCSI or local nvme backed by replication).
- batch/aux (2–4 x CPU nodes) — offline jobs, snapshotting, image build.

I'll attach a short list of ops questions for your team to fill out (initial-ops-questions.md). Can your ops-manager pick a 90-minute window next week for an on-site preflight or remote walkthrough?

— Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Deployment Engineering
Redwood Inference

Rishi — quick answers inline: 

> 1) Egress proxy: is mutual TLS to the proxy supported from a host agent? will the proxy allow long-lived outbound connections for our control-plane tunnel (typically a TLS reverse-tunnel)?
Yes — proxy supports mTLS from host clients. Long-lived outbound TLS tunnels are allowed from the management VLAN; prod racks must route via the proxy.

> 2) HSM integration: can your ops team provision a KMS endpoint reachable from the management VLAN only, or do we need an HSM appliance directly on the control-plane hosts?
We have an HSM appliance available on the management VLAN (not in the prod racks). Network ACLs can restrict access to a small subset of hosts.

> 3) Rack power/thermal: GPUs planned per rack? you mentioned 4x GPUs per 10U earlier in the doc — can you confirm GPU model families?
We are provisioning 4x Nvidia A40-style GPUs per 10U slot. Power has been reviewed and we can sustain that density.

> 4) Backup window: how often are cross-room SAN snapshots permitted (hourly/daily)?
SAN snapshots are nightly by default; we can run an hourly snapshot job during the preflight window but it will be throttled.

Attaching the floor plan for room A (floorplan-dc-A.pdf). For storage preference: we prefer using local NVMe for model KV cache and use iSCSI-backed blockstore for model artifacts that require replication across rooms. We need encryption-at-rest and KMS-backed key rotation.

Thanks — ops-manager will propose times for the on-site preflight.

— Emily

Subject: Re: StrataGrid site questionnaire and initial constraints — recommended on‑prem reference architecture

Emily / Rishi — based on the constraints above, here is a recommended on-prem reference architecture and a short preflight checklist. This is intentionally conservative to reduce surprises during the cutover.

Reference architecture (high level):
- Control plane placement: deploy a 3-node control-plane inside the management VLAN (non-routable from prod racks). Control plane runs etcd, operator control services, and the secure tunnel endpoint for the Redwood Private control-plane connector. No public IPs.
- Data plane (customer cluster): GPU nodepools in prod racks; each GPU node should have local NVMe (for KV cache + ephemeral slices) and an iSCSI path to the replicated blockstore for model weights. Use node labels/taints: node.k8s.redwood/role=inference, node.k8s.redwood/gpu=true.
- Network segmentation: separate VLANs for management, control-plane, and prod. Egress from prod must go through the proxy in DMZ; control-plane traffic to HSM/KMS limited by ACLs. Pod network can be Calico with IPIP disabled; enable eBPF dataplane if supported to reduce CPU overhead.
- Storage classes and CSI recommendations:
  - sc-fast-local (provisioner: local-volume) -> for KV cache (use ext4/XFS on NVMe, no replication, expect next-token eviction resiliency).
  - sc-blockstore (provisioner: iscsi-csi) -> for model weights, backed by SAN replication across rooms; enable write-through caching and set replication factor = 2.
  - sc-shared (provisioner: nfs-subdir-external-provisioner) -> for small shared artifacts (configs, licenses).
- Encryption and keys: integrate with your HSM/KMS using the KMIP or vault-agent pattern. Control-plane secrets encrypted using KMS keys; CSI driver should support KMS-encrypted volumes or use LUKS on block devices with KMS-managed keys.

Sizing guidance (first phase):
- control-plane: 3 x 8 vCPU, 32 GiB RAM, 200 GB SSD each (redundant etcd, anti-affinity across rooms).
- inference-gpu nodes: start with 6 nodes, each with 4x A40-style GPUs, 512 GiB RAM, 2x 1.6 TB NVMe (one for OS+KV, one for local scratch), 16 TB blockstore mount available via iSCSI.
- batch/aux: 3 x 16 vCPU, 64 GiB RAM for builds and snapshot jobs.

Networking specifics (firewall ports):
- Control-plane <-> Data-plane: TCP 8443 (API), 2379–2380 (etcd), 10250 (kubelet) — restrict to specific hosts.
- Tunnel/outbound: 443 outbound to Redwood control endpoint (over the proxy).
- NTP and DNS: ensure prod racks can reach internal NTP servers and DNS resolvers.

Operational runbook highlights:
1) Preflight: validate rack power, swap temp sensors, verify HSM network ACLs, confirm proxy mTLS cert distribution.
2) Image signing: require signed node images; we can help validate checksums during onboarding.
3) Backup: daily snapshots for model weights with hourly delta snapshots during initial training imports. Test restore to a staging room before cutover.
4) Upgrade path: test K8s minor upgrades in an isolated staging Vlan, do canary upgrades of inference nodepools with rolling restart.

Constraints/risks and mitigations:
- Risk: SAN write latency spikes affecting model weight writes -> mitigate with write-through caching on the node and async replication to SAN.
- Risk: Air-gap complicates control-plane telemetry -> we recommend a pull-based diagnostics bundle that can be exported on schedule via ops-manager.

Next steps:
- Ops: fill the attached initial-ops-questions.md and provide kernel versions and NIC driver details for the GPU servers.
- Schedule: propose two candidate 90-minute windows for the on-site preflight; we prefer the earlier of the two for hardware access.

I'll attach a reference diagram (redwood-onprem-reference-arch.drawio). Happy to jump on the preflight call and walk the room floorplan.

— Irene Choi
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
